current_answer: As of 17 September 2026 at 12:00 UTC, no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven. The strongest fresh movement is in usable access and allowance economics: an open Codex report says three ordinary travel-search messages used about 73% of a five-hour Plus window, while OpenAI documents plan-, model-, and workspace-dependent limits and possible fallback. That is a credible user-facing access/economics lead, not proof that model weights declined. The earlier account-capacity-conditioned Astra quality lead remains credible but its served model is unknown; fresh context, product, safety-disclosure, and benchmark evidence keep the lanes separate.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: No broad model collapse is proven. Three ordinary travel-search messages reportedly used about 73% of a five-hour Plus window; call that an access/economics lead, not a weight verdict.

summary: No broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven; the fresh lead is a usable-access and allowance-economics problem.
Open Codex issue #45510 reports about 73% of a five-hour Plus window consumed by three ordinary travel-search messages, without a provider ledger or full trace.
OpenAI documents plan-, model-, and workspace-dependent limits, separate Work and Codex allowances, and possible fallback; this explains why allowance pressure is not a weight verdict.
Windows Guardian and sandbox issues show product or execution failures before work runs, while provider status pages show resolved or absent incidents in separate availability lanes.
OpenAI’s safety disclosure and live benchmark boards answer different questions; individual safety cases and cross-sectional scores do not establish broad production decline.
Community reports make capacity shock, switching pressure, and lost work salient, but remain self-selected; the reader still needs a route-and-outcome receipt.
Reader move: record requested and served model, route, capacity, context, effort, tool trace, artifact, self-check, allowance movement, and recovered work before switching.
uncertainty: The 73% allowance report is one self-selected issue with three ordinary messages, no provider ledger, no complete tool trace, and no completed-task quality measure.
OpenAI guidance documents limit and fallback rules but does not reveal an individual account route, effective model, or capacity state.
The Astra capacity-quality report remains one account with two pre-event and six post-event runs, a noisy SVG task, and unknown served model.
Status pages and the safety framework are provider records with different estimands; they do not establish silent routing, production prevalence, or ordinary task quality.
Benchmark boards are cross-sectional or harness-specific, community threads are self-selected, and no representative denominator, recovered-time measure, or willingness-to-pay evidence is available.
freshness_note: Fresh public-source research completed 17 September 2026. The center of gravity moved from the prior narrow Astra capacity-quality lead toward a more general usable-window and allowance-economics lead, while missing ledgers, route provenance, controls, and prevalence keep broad capability decline unproven.
